title: A Randomised Controlled Study on Hourly Surgical–Anaesthesia Check-ins to Improve Intraoperative Team Communication (BRIDGE-Trial)
summary:
Major visceral surgical procedures require continuous coordination between surgical and anaesthesia teams. Effective intraoperative communication is essential to maintain a shared understanding of the operative status, patient condition and anticipated next steps. The BRIDGE trial investigates whether brief, structured, hourly surgical–anaesthesia check-ins improve intraoperative team communication and perceived interprofessional collaboration during major visceral surgical procedures.

Adult patients scheduled for elective visceral surgical procedures with an expected duration of more than four hours will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either standard intraoperative communication or standard communication plus hourly BRIDGE check-ins. The control group will receive standard care including the routine team time-out and sign-out. In the intervention group, the surgical and anaesthesia teams will additionally perform brief structured check-ins at hourly intervals using a predefined five-question framework. After surgery, both the responsible surgeon and anaesthesiologist will complete a short Team Satisfaction Questionnaire. Secondary outcomes include postoperative complications up to postoperative day 30, operating room and anaesthesia times, and intraoperative deviations in vital parameters.

The intervention does not involve additional invasive procedures, blood sampling or imaging for participating patients.
conditions: Intraoperative communication, interdisciplinary collaboration, patient safety, operating room teamwork

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Conventional and minimally invasive visceral surgical abdominal procedures  
- Planned operative duration > 4 hours  
- Age ≥ 18 years
Exclusion criteria:
- Operative duration < 4 hours  
- Thoracic procedures  
- Participation in other studies that could potentially influence the study results
